title: The Boston Pops date with Getz
summary: Under-rehearsed sight reading makes it a disaster.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I thought that was a disaster, the band sight reading it.

What they give a symphony orchestra is nothing, they run it down twice. The conductor really didn't know what was going on, and Stan didn't either. He gets up on the stage (inaudible), so he begins to read what I have on the sheet and all I had written down was just a guide, but he played what I wrote. How
could it have life? It's good for what it might have been, but not for jazz.
Were you there to rehearse the orchestra?
No, I was there in case Fiedler wanted to ask a question.
My own limited experience with bringing things in--
I have to be there to rehearse whatever our combo is doing, because whenever I'm not there--
That's right, so that's what happened there. So I rarely play that thing.
I did a movie the guy couldn't sell and nobody got paid.
Felicia, and that turned out good. I had all the Sauter-Pinegan guys and a great string section.
